quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Drive at the same speed as the other traffic (if they are following the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot crash into each other. Most multi-vehicle crashes happen when vehicles are driving at different speeds.

questions.question: There may be times when 10 mph is too fast for drivers to safely operate their vehicles.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions require it. Bad traffic, weather, or visibility may mean you need to drive as slow as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light without stopping. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A single broken white line on a highway means:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a white dashed line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs show?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive faster than a train to cross ahead of it.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if the maneuver is done slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before leaving a curb to warn other drivers.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small vehicle, you should be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer correctly when passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers that bicycles may cross at this location.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Make constant visual checks.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make constant visual checks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss in your blind spots or when looking quickly. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: Why is double parking not allowed?

options.text: The driver is illegally avoiding parking fees.
It blocks traffic and causes accidents.
Your car may roll into traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It blocks traffic and causes accidents.
questions.explanation: Double parking is parking on the street side of a car that is already parked at the curb. It is not allowed because it blocks traffic and can cause accidents.

questions.question: To avoid being blinded by headlights from oncoming cars:

options.text: Focus your eyes on the centerline of the road.
Glance to the right side of the road.
Focus your eyes straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look back and forth between the right side of the road and the road ahead. This helps you avoid the glare from oncoming headlights while staying safely in your lane.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirror. This is dangerous because you lose your safety space if the truck stops suddenly. Always keep extra distance between you and a truck.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder and make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Never try to pass or change lanes in an intersection.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, you should:

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, return to the right lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you just passed.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under bad weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you interrupt the normal flow of traffic. You can get a ticket for driving too slowly.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus when its red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out. This law applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic behind and to the side of your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your low beam headlights:

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Always use low beam headlights when driving in fog. High beam headlights reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you have more than one hazard, deal with one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: You see a "Merging traffic" sign on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Honk at the incoming traffic.
Always stay at your current speed.
Speed up to avoid slowing traffic.
Change lanes, if it is safe, to let traffic merge in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes, if it is safe, to let traffic merge in.
questions.explanation: When you are on a road with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering the freeway. If no one is next to you, move to another lane.

questions.question: A school bus ahead is stopped to pick up or drop off children. What must you do?

options.text: Stop completely until all children have left the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in.
Change lanes and drive slowly past the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm retracts before you go. Even when the bus starts moving, do not go until you know no children are crossing in front of you.

questions.question: When you increase your vehicle's speed, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes cross traffic easier to see.
It does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, your vision narrows. You must stay alert to dangers.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will get worse. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do when you reach a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop unless a police officer tells you otherwise. Look and yield the right-of-way before you enter.
